title_en: Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop v. Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: China's Trademark Law encourages producers and operators to ensure the quality of goods and services through honest business operations, establish a reputation consistent with their own business credit, continuously enhance the brand value of their trademarks, and at the same time protect the interests of consumers, producers, and operators. Citizens enjoy their legitimate right to name and may naturally use their own names reasonably. However, when a citizen uses his or her name as a trademark or enterprise name for commercial purposes, it must not violate the principle of good faith or infringe upon the prior rights of others. Where a person, knowing that another person's registered trademark or enterprise name enjoys high reputation and influence, still registers an enterprise name identical to that of another person, and prominently uses a trademark or enterprise name identical or similar to the other person's registered trademark on the same or similar goods or services, it is evident that such person has the malicious intent to free-ride on the reputation of the other person's registered trademark or enterprise name, which is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public. Such conduct does not constitute a reasonable use of a name, and constitutes infringement of another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark and unfair competition.

full_text_en:
Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop v. Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition

Ruling Summary

The Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China encourages producers and business operators to guarantee the quality of goods and services through honest business operations, to establish popularity commensurate with their own commercial reputation, and to continuously enhance the brand value of their trademarks, while at the same time protecting the interests of consumers, producers, and business operators. Citizens enjoy their lawful right to a name and may, of course, reasonably use their own names. However, when a citizen uses his or her name as a trademark or corporate name for commercial purposes, such use must not violate the principle of good faith or infringe upon the prior rights of others. Where a person knowingly uses a corporate name identical to another's corporate name, or prominently uses a trademark or corporate name identical or similar to another's registered trademark in the same or similar goods or services, despite knowing that the other party's registered trademark or corporate name enjoys high popularity and influence, such conduct clearly shows malicious intent to ride on the popularity of the other party's registered trademark or corporate name and is likely to cause confusion among relevant members of the public. Such conduct does not constitute fair use of one's name but rather constitutes infringement of another's exclusive right to use a registered trademark and unfair competition.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 238

Petitioner for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop. Domicile: No. 178, South Avenue of Xinjiekou, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Gao Wenhui, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Ma Xiang, attorney at Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yanfeng, attorney at Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 101, Yard No. 2000, Tianchen Road, High-tech Zone, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Qingfeng, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jia Mingjun, attorney at Shandong Deheng (Jinan) Law Firm.

The petitioner for retrial, Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop (hereinafter referred to as Qingfeng Baozi Shop), filed an application for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (2014) Lu Min San Zhong Zi No. 43 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance) in the case of a dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition with the respondent, Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingfeng Catering Company). This Court rendered the civil ruling (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 205 on December 28, 2015, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing in this case. The agents ad litem of the petitioner Qingfeng Baozi Shop, Ma Xiang and Liu Yanfeng, and the legal representative of the respondent, Xu Qingfeng, and the agent ad litem Jia Mingjun appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

Qingfeng Baozi Shop submitted the following grounds for retrial: 1. "Qingfeng" is the prior corporate name and registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop, with strong distinctiveness, and should be protected by law. Beijing Xicheng District Catering Company Xuannei Catering Basic Unit Qingfeng Baozi Shop was established in 1956 at No. 122, West Chang'an Street, Beijing. Its name was successively changed to "Beijing Xicheng District Catering Company Qingfeng Baozi Shop" and "Beijing Xicheng District Qingfeng Baozi Shop." On July 24, 2007, it changed to its current name, with its address changed to No. 178, South Avenue of Xinjiekou, Xicheng District, Beijing. The enterprise nature has always been state-owned, mainly engaged in traditional Beijing snacks such as noodles, baozi (steamed stuffed buns), and chaogan (stir-fried liver). The trademark No. 1171838 "Qingfeng" (in Chinese characters) of Qingfeng Baozi Shop was registered on January 28, 1998, designated for use on services in Class 42 (now Class 43); its trademark No. 3201612 "Lao Qingfeng + laoqingfeng" was registered on July 21, 2003, designated for use on goods in Class 30. Qingfeng Catering Company was established on June 24, 2009, with a business scope of catering management and consulting. "Qingfeng," as the corporate name and registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop, has strong distinctiveness, and its registration and use far predate the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company. The prior rights should be protected by law. 2. Qingfeng Baozi Shop is a representative of traditional Beijing snacks and a popular tourist attraction nationwide. "Qingfeng" has become a well-known time-honored brand in China, enjoying high popularity and reputation and being widely known by the relevant public. "Qingfeng" has been used on the shop sign since its opening 58 years ago. In May 2014, it was recognized as a "Beijing Time-honored Brand" by the Beijing Time-honored Brand Association. Qingfeng Baozi Shop has always been operating traditional Beijing snacks and actively exploring the development of "traditional snacks." It invested heavily to establish the first Beijing snack factory, set up a research and development center, and achieved standardization, normalization, and factory production of Beijing snacks. It became one of the first Beijing snack catering enterprises to pass the ISO9001 quality management system and ISO22000 food safety management system certifications. Qingfeng Baozi Shop also actively expanded through chain stores and franchise outlets, opening Qingfeng Baozi Shop branches both in and outside Beijing. By the time Qingfeng Catering Company was established on June 24, 2009, it had already opened more than 100 branches, and by now it has 267 branches. Its geographic coverage includes Beijing, Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Shandong, Tianjin, and other provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government. From 2007 to 2009, Qingfeng Baozi Shop's turnover was RMB 800 million; from 2007 to 2013, the turnover was RMB 3 billion; from 2009 to 2013, its average annual turnover and market share ranked second nationally, making it one of the largest traditional snack enterprises in China. Qingfeng Baozi Shop has received honors such as "China's Top Ten Chain Catering Enterprises," "China's Specialty Restaurant," "Beijing Top 50 Catering Enterprises," "Beijing Honest Business Enterprise," "Breakfast Project Demonstration Shop," and "Top Ten Most Popular Restaurants Among Foodies." Qingfeng Baozi Shop and Qingfeng baozi (steamed stuffed buns), with their long history, good quality, Beijing characteristics, and wide and dense distribution, have become a representative snack in Beijing, a specialty snack for out-of-town tourists visiting Beijing, and a "popular tourist attraction nationwide." Qingfeng Baozi Shop also attaches importance to brand promotion, spending a large amount on advertising each year, and had already gained high popularity before the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company. From 2007 to 2009, the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce recognized "Qingfeng" as a famous trademark; in 2011, "Qingfeng" was rated as "Beijing Top Ten Catering Brands"; in 2012 and 2014, "Qingfeng" was rated as "Most Consumer-Approved Brand at the China Baozi Culture Festival"; in 2010 and 2013, "Qingfeng" was twice recognized as a "Beijing Well-Known Trademark." Beijing has well-developed transportation, and its radiation range covers the whole country. Especially in the Internet age, information dissemination has no geographic restrictions. The relevant public in Shandong can learn about the "Qingfeng" corporate name and trademark through various channels. A large number of consumers in Shandong dine at Qingfeng Baozi Shop every year. Shandong media have also reported on "Qingfeng." The service territory of Qingfeng Baozi Shop has long been not limited to Beijing; "Qingfeng" has become widely known by consumers, and its influence has extended to Shandong, the place of registration of Qingfeng Catering Company. The court of second instance erred in limiting the scope of protection of the registered trademark by the regional nature of the designated services, violating the principle of nationwide protection of registered trademarks under the Trademark Law. 3. Before the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company, its legal representative, Xu Qingfeng, had been engaged in catering services in Beijing for a long time, operating the canteen of Beijing University of Technology. There were three Qingfeng Baozi Shop branches near Beijing University of Technology: the Wusheng store opened on June 13, 2008, the Dawang Road store opened on November 23, 2008, and the Fatou store opened on January 1, 2009. Qingfeng Baozi Shop has strong influence in the industry. Xu Qingfeng could not have been unaware of the popularity of the trademark and corporate name of Qingfeng Baozi Shop, yet he used the "Qingfeng" corporate name to establish a catering company and imitated the trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop by prominently using it on its official website, storefront, menu, and advertising materials. Subjectively, he had malicious intent to ride on the goodwill. His use of the "Qingfeng" or "Qingfeng Catering" signs constituted trademark use. The court of second instance erred in finding that this constituted non-prominent use of an abbreviation or corporate name. The prominent use of the "Qingfeng" trademark and corporate name by Qingfeng Catering Company is likely to cause confusion and misidentification among the relevant public, constituting trademark infringement; its registration and use of "Qingfeng" as a corporate name for operating identical or similar services constitutes unfair competition. It requested the court to: 1. Revoke the judgments of first and second instances; 2. Order Qingfeng Catering Company to immediately cease the infringement, including but not limited to destroying any door signs, plaques, price lists, name cards, posters, and other advertisements bearing the "Qingfeng" mark, and deleting the "Qingfeng" mark from its website; 3. Order Qingfeng Catering Company to immediately cease using the corporate name containing the words "Qingfeng" and to change its corporate name within a specified period; 4. Order Qingfeng Catering Company to publish a statement in the Jinan Daily to eliminate the adverse effects; 5. Order Qingfeng Catering Company to compensate Qingfeng Baozi Shop for economic losses and reasonable expenses of RMB 500,000; 6. Order Qingfeng Catering Company to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Qingfeng Catering Company did not submit a written defense.

Qingfeng Baozi Shop filed a lawsuit with the Jinan Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance), requesting a judgment ordering Qingfeng Catering Company to: 1. Immediately cease the trademark infringement, including removing and destroying plaques, signs, price lists, name cards, and other materials bearing the "Qingfeng" mark, and deleting the promotional use of the "Qingfeng" mark online; 2. Immediately cease using the corporate name containing the "Qingfeng" characters; 3. Publish a statement in the Jinan Daily to eliminate adverse effects; 4. Compensate Qingfeng Baozi Shop for economic losses of RMB 500,000 and for attorneys' fees, notarization fees, and investigation and evidence collection fees of RMB 90,000.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On June 3, 1986, the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a business license to Beijing Xicheng District Catering Company Qingfeng Baozi Shop, indicating its business address as No. 122, West Chang'an Street, economic nature as state-owned, accounting form as independent accounting, opening date as 1956, business method as retail, and business scope as noodles. On May 15, 2000, the Xicheng Sub-bureau of the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a business license for a legal person enterprise to Beijing Xicheng District Qingfeng Baozi Shop, indicating its business address as No. 85, Xi'anmen Street, economic nature as state-owned ownership, establishment date as January 5, 1982, and business scope as noodles (including liquid foods, cold meats, cold dishes), retail wine and beverages. On July 24, 2007, Beijing Xicheng District Qingfeng Baozi Shop was approved to change its name to Qingfeng Baozi Shop. Beijing Huatian Catering Group Company is the administrative department of Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

On January 28, 1998, Beijing Huatian Catering Group Company obtained the registration of the trademark "Qingfeng" (in Chinese characters), Trademark Registration Certificate No. 1171838, designated for use on services in Class 42 (now Class 43): restaurants, temporary dining rooms, self-service dining rooms, fast food restaurants, and cafes. On August 14, 2008, the trademark was approved to change the registrant name to Qingfeng Baozi Shop, and upon renewal, the validity period was from April 28, 2008, to April 27, 2018.

On July 21, 2003, Beijing Xicheng District Qingfeng Baozi Shop obtained the registration of the trademark "Lao Qingfeng + laoqingfeng," Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3201612, designated for use on goods in Class 30: instant noodles, pastries, bread, dumplings, Chinese flatbread, steamed buns, yuanxiao (glutinous rice balls), sweet bean paste, baozi, and mutton soup with crispy bread. On November 13, 2008, the trademark was approved to change the registrant name to Qingfeng Baozi Shop, and upon renewal, the validity period was from July 21, 2013, to July 20, 2023.

The Yuetan store of Qingfeng Baozi Shop was recognized as a "Chinese Specialty Restaurant" by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Commerce in 2007. In 2007, Qingfeng Baozi Shop spent RMB 1,316,604 on advertising on Beijing Radio and Beijing Television. From 2008 to June 20, 2009, Qingfeng Baozi Shop spent RMB 3,222,500 on advertising on the above media. On July 7, 2006, the New Beijing Daily featured an introduction to Qingfeng Baozi Shop in its entertainment section. On February 4, 2009, Qingfeng Baozi Shop entered into a franchise contract with Wang Na for a business location at Floor 1, Building 1, Guanzhuang Xili, Chaoyang District, Beijing, with the store name Beijing Guanzhuang Qingfeng Baozi Shop, a one-time franchise fee of RMB 100,000, and an annual Qingfeng brand usage fee of RMB 60,000. On December 22, 2009, Qingfeng Baozi Shop entered into a franchise contract with Yang Jun for a business location at Floor 1, No. A8, Chedaogou, Haidian District, Beijing, with the store name Beijing Junle Qingfeng Baozi Shop, a one-time franchise fee of RMB 100,000, and an annual Qingfeng brand usage fee of RMB 60,000.

On June 24, 2009, Qingfeng Catering Company was registered and established, with legal representative Xu Qingfeng, registered capital of RMB 500,000, company type as a limited liability company (invested or controlled by natural persons), business scope as catering management and consulting, and with three natural persons as shareholders, of which Xu Qingfeng contributed RMB 350,000, accounting for 70%. On July 23, 2013, at the request of Qingfeng Baozi Shop, the Beijing Zhongxin Notary Office performed evidence preservation by logging onto the website of Qingfeng Catering Company, www.qingfengcanyin.com, and issued a notarial certificate (2013) Jing Zhongxin Nei Jing Zheng Zi No. 18419. The notarial certificate recorded that the website of Qingfeng Catering Company had columns such as "Entering Qingfeng," "Qingfeng Culture," "Qingfeng Highlights," and "Qingfeng News." From July 15, 2009, to August 26, 2012, Qingfeng Catering Company operated in-house canteens for eight enterprises, including Jili Restaurant. On June 4, 2010, the restaurant of Jinan Jili Automobile Co., Ltd. opened, and Qingfeng Catering Company displayed a banner reading "Qingfeng Catering Staff Welcomes You."

The court of first instance held that in traditional Chinese business culture, merchants tend to choose words with auspicious and festive meanings as their corporate names or trademarks. From the perspective of the commercial identification rights of corporate names or trademarks, such corporate names or trademarks do not have strong inherent distinctiveness; rather, they rely on the subsequent use and maintenance by the merchant to give them specific meanings and establish a specific connection with the merchant. The infringements alleged by Qingfeng Baozi Shop against Qingfeng Catering Company in this case include two types: 1. Qingfeng Catering Company's registration and use of the corporate name "Jinan Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd." infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop; 2. Qingfeng Catering Company's creation of a column "Entering Qingfeng" on its website and display of a banner reading "Qingfeng Catering Staff Welcomes You" at its business premises infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop. With respect to the second type of alleged infringement, since Qingfeng Catering Company used the words "Qingfeng" consistently with their context and did not prominently use them in terms of font, size, or color, this constituted a reasonable use of the abbreviation or corporate name. Therefore, the focus of this case was whether the first type of alleged infringement by Qingfeng Baozi Shop was established, that is, whether the registration and use of the corporate name "Jinan Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd." by Qingfeng Catering Company infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop. A trademark is a commercial mark that distinguishes the source of goods or services, consisting of elements such as words or graphics. Registered trademarks are approved by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, and the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is effective nationwide. A corporate name is a mark that distinguishes market entities, consisting of four parts in order: the administrative division where the enterprise is located, the trade name, the industry or operational characteristics, and the organizational form. Among these, the trade name is the main mark distinguishing different enterprises. The exclusive right of an enterprise to use its corporate name and trade name is limited by the administrative division and industry or operational characteristics specified in the approval of its corporate name. Due to the differences in the approving bodies and approval procedures for registered trademarks and corporate names, conflicts between words in registered trademarks and trade names in corporate names are inevitable. Whether such conflicts are lawful must be determined on a case-by-case basis in accordance with the law. In this case, Qingfeng Catering Company began registering and using the corporate name "Jinan Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd." on June 24, 2009, and its business territory was Jinan. The two trademarks involved were approved on January 28, 1998, and July 21, 2003, respectively. Qingfeng Baozi Shop acquired the two trademarks on August 14, 2008, and November 13, 2008, respectively. Qingfeng Baozi Shop had no evidence to prove that at the time Qingfeng Catering Company registered and used the alleged corporate name, Qingfeng Baozi Shop's business territory and goodwill had already extended to or affected Jinan and Shandong, nor did it have evidence to prove that Qingfeng Catering Company registered and used the alleged corporate name with the possibility of borrowing the goodwill of Qingfeng Baozi Shop's trademarks. At the same time, the existing evidence provided by Qingfeng Baozi Shop could not prove that the relevant public had misidentified or was likely to misidentify Qingfeng Baozi Shop with Qingfeng Catering Company. Therefore, the registration and use of the corporate name "Jinan Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd." by Qingfeng Catering Company was reasonable and did not infringe upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

The court of first instance rendered the following judgment: In accordance with Article 51 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, and Article 3 of the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration, it was adjudged as follows: The claims of Qingfeng Baozi Shop were dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 9,700 was borne by Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Qingfeng Baozi Shop appealed to the court of second instance, requesting that the first-instance judgment be revoked and a new judgment be entered in its favor. The main reasons were: The court of first instance erred in finding the facts and applying the law. 1. Qingfeng Catering Company's use of the "Qingfeng" trade name alone at its business premises and on its website constituted prominent use of "Qingfeng" and infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark involved. 2. Qingfeng Catering Company's act of using the words "Qingfeng," which were identical to the registered trademark involved, as its corporate name and using it was done with subjective malice and constituted unfair competition. 3. The court of first instance erred in finding that Qingfeng Baozi Shop had no evidence to prove that its business territory and goodwill had extended to Shandong and that the actions of Qingfeng Catering Company would not cause confusion among the relevant public. 4. This case should be governed by the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademark Disputes and other laws and judicial interpretations. The court of first instance erred in applying the Measures for the Implementation of the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. Qingfeng Catering Company responded, arguing that the court of first instance correctly found the facts and applied the law and requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld.

During the second instance, Qingfeng Baozi Shop submitted the following evidence to prove the high reputation of the trademark in question in Shandong and nationwide: 1. Certificate from Beijing Cuisine Association; 2. Audit reports of Qingfeng Baozi Shop for 2009-2013; 3. Attached maps showing the development of Qingfeng Baozi Shop chain stores over the years; 4. Franchise contracts signed between Qingfeng Baozi Shop and franchisees; 5. Pre-franchise intention forms for Qingfeng from other provinces and cities; 6. Applicant information forms; 7. Franchise consultation records; 8. Reports on Qingfeng Baozi Shop in the Jinan Times, Qilu Evening News, Life Daily, etc.; 9. Records of infringement information on the Qingfeng trademark; 10. Cases of proactive law enforcement by industry and commerce authorities. Qingfeng Catering Company challenged the evidence, stating that it disputed the authenticity of evidence items 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 10; did not dispute the authenticity of evidence item 2 but argued it was irrelevant to this case; did not dispute the authenticity of evidence item 4 but argued it only proved the franchise situation in the Beijing area and could not prove the situation in Shandong; did not dispute the authenticity of evidence item 8 but argued that the reports were dated after 2013 and were irrelevant to this case; did not dispute the authenticity of the photos of the alleged infringement in evidence item 9 but argued they were irrelevant to this case. The court of second instance held that evidence items 1 and 4 could only prove the reputation of Qingfeng Baozi Shop in the Beijing area and could not prove the reputation of the trademark in question in Shandong and nationwide; evidence item 2 was irrelevant to the reputation of the trademark in question; evidence items 3, 5, 6, 7, and 10 were all produced by Qingfeng Baozi Shop itself, and their authenticity could not be confirmed; the time of formation of evidence item 8 was after the alleged infringing act occurred and could not prove the reputation of the trademark at the time of the alleged infringing act; evidence item 9 only indicated that a third party used "Qingfeng" as its trade name and was irrelevant to this case. In summary, the above evidence submitted by Qingfeng Baozi Shop lacked probative force for its intended proof, and the court of second instance did not admit it.

The court of second instance found the facts as follows: The facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the focus of the dispute between the parties in this case was: whether the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company infringed the trademark rights in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop; and whether the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company constituted unfair competition.

Regarding the issue of whether the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company infringed the trademark rights in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop. Qingfeng Baozi Shop claimed that the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company were: using the words "Qingfeng Catering" (庆丰餐饮), "Entering Qingfeng" (走进庆丰), "Qingfeng Culture" (庆丰文化) and similar on its website; using the words "Qingfeng Catering welcomes all employees" (庆丰餐饮全体员工欢迎您) at its business premises; and using the words "Qingfeng Catering" on employee uniforms and business cards. Qingfeng Baozi Shop argued that the above acts of Qingfeng Catering Company infringed its trademark rights in question. Article 52, item (1) of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China provides that using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the permission of the trademark registrant constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. Article 9, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks provides that trademark similarity means that the accused trademark, when compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, is similar in the shape, pronunciation, or meaning of characters, or the composition and color of graphics, or the overall structure after the combination of their respective elements, such that it is likely to cause the relevant public to be confused about the source of the goods or to believe that the source of the goods has a specific connection with the goods of the plaintiff's registered trademark. Article 10 of that Interpretation provides that in determining whether a trademark is similar, consideration shall be given to the distinctiveness and reputation of the registered trademark sought to be protected. In this case, Qingfeng Baozi Shop claimed protection for two trademarks: the traditional Chinese character "慶豐" word mark and the simplified Chinese character "老庆丰+lao qing feng" word-phonetic mark. The court of second instance held that, first, when Qingfeng Catering Company used the characters "庆丰", it did not highlight them in terms of font, size, or color, but rather used them reasonably as an abbreviation or trade name of its enterprise name. Second, comparing the accused infringing mark "庆丰" with the traditional Chinese character "慶豐" word mark, the differences were significant, and they did not constitute identical marks; comparing the accused infringing mark "庆丰" with the simplified Chinese character "老庆丰+lao qing feng" word-phonetic mark, the accused infringing mark was only identical to the "庆丰" part of the trademark, but not identical to the other characters and phonetic parts. Finally, based on the evidence submitted by Qingfeng Baozi Shop, the reputation of the trademarks in question was mainly limited to the Beijing area, and it failed to prove that the trademarks in question had a high reputation in Shandong and Jinan at the time of the alleged infringing act. In summary, the accused infringing mark was not identical or similar to the trademarks in question and would not cause the relevant public to be confused about the source of the goods or to believe that the source had a specific connection with the goods of the registered trademarks in question. The alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company did not infringe the trademarks in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

Regarding the issue of whether the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company constituted unfair competition. Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides that business operators in market transactions shall follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, honesty, and good faith, and comply with generally accepted business ethics. The court of second instance held that, first, the trademarks in question were the traditional Chinese character "慶豐" word mark and the simplified Chinese character "老庆丰+lao qing feng" word-phonetic mark, and the enterprise trade name "庆丰" of Qingfeng Catering Company was not identical to those trademarks. Second, Qingfeng Baozi Shop failed to provide evidence proving that its trademarks in question had a high reputation in Shandong and Jinan at the time when Qingfeng Catering Company used "庆丰" as its enterprise trade name. Therefore, Qingfeng Catering Company did not subjectively intend to ride on the goodwill of the Qingfeng Baozi Shop trademark; objectively, it would not cause confusion or mistake among the relevant public; and it did not violate principles such as honesty and good faith, nor did it constitute unfair competition. Additionally, the court of first instance erred in failing to apply the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China in its judgment, and the court of second instance corrected this.

The court of second instance ruled: the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 9,700 was to be borne by Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

Upon retrial by this court, it was found that: when Qingfeng Catering Company was approved and registered on June 24, 2009, its name was Jinan Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd., and it changed to its current name on September 3, 2014.

Regarding the retrial requests of the parties, this court determined the disputed evidence and facts as follows:

During the retrial, Qingfeng Baozi Shop submitted the following evidence: 1. Franchise contracts, to prove that since 2008, Qingfeng Baozi Shop had licensed Yuan Guibin and others to use the "庆丰" mark to operate Qingfeng Baozi Shop near Beijing University of Technology; 2. Special audit report of Qingfeng Baozi Shop issued by Beijing Dezheng Certified Public Accountants, to prove that from 2009 to 2013, the turnover of Qingfeng Baozi Shop was RMB 200.68 million, 278.52 million, 364.87 million, 436.41 million, and 519.29 million respectively; that there were a total of 293 directly operated and franchised "庆丰" stores, distributed in Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, and elsewhere; that media publicity coverage was nationwide, with a total advertising expenditure of RMB 10.43 million; 3. Trademark archives, to prove that on September 16, 2013, Qingfeng Catering Company applied for registration of trademarks containing the characters "庆丰" in Class 30 for goods such as "steamed buns" and in Class 43 for services such as "restaurants, eateries, fast food restaurants," demonstrating its consistent free-riding behavior; 4. Trademark archives, to prove that on August 7, 2007, Qingfeng Baozi Shop applied for registration of a "Q" graphic mark, and that the graphic mark used by Qingfeng Catering Company was also an imitation of Qingfeng Baozi Shop's graphic mark; 5. An article published on Xinhua website titled "Inspur Invests RMB 1.2 Billion to Build a Science and Technology Park in Jinan," to prove that Beijing Inspur Group established Jinan Inspur Company in Jinan, and that Qingfeng Catering Company operated a "Qingfeng" restaurant within Jinan Inspur Company, where many employees came from Beijing, which could easily cause confusion among the relevant public.

Qingfeng Catering Company expressed the following opinions on the above evidence: For evidence 1, Xu Qingfeng's restaurant was located at another campus of Beijing University of Technology and only operated in Beijing for three or four months; for evidence 2, the authenticity of the audit report was admitted; for evidence 3, the authenticity was admitted; for evidence 4, Qingfeng Catering Company could register other trademarks, and Qingfeng Baozi Shop's claim that they were similar to its trademarks went beyond the scope of this case; for evidence 5, Inspur Group was not registered in Beijing, and the evidence could not achieve the purpose of proof.

This court certified the above evidence submitted by Qingfeng Baozi Shop as follows: The authenticity of evidence items 1-5 was all admitted. Evidence 1 could prove that Qingfeng Baozi Shop opened a branch near Beijing University of Technology; evidence 2 could prove the business situation of Qingfeng Baozi Shop from 2009 to 2013; evidence items 3-4 could prove the registration status of the trademarks, but were irrelevant to this case; evidence 5 was not related to this case and could not prove the fact that Qingfeng Catering Company operated a "Qingfeng" restaurant within Jinan Inspur Company or that some employees came from Beijing.

During the retrial, Qingfeng Catering Company submitted a certificate from Shandong Songqiao Catering Management Co., Ltd., showing that: Xu Qingfeng joined the company in November 2007 and was later sent to Gengdan College of Beijing University of Technology, located in Shunyi District, Beijing, to study restaurant management. The company arranged for him to return to Jinan in April 2008 and assigned him to Jinan Engineering Vocational and Technical College for restaurant management. He left the company on October 10, 2008. Qingfeng Baozi Shop challenged the evidence, stating that it admitted its authenticity but disputed its relevance. The evidence was a certificate issued by a company, not from an administrative authority, and constituted witness testimony, which could not achieve the purpose of proof. In this regard, this court held that the above evidence submitted by Qingfeng Catering Company, combined with the opinions expressed by Qingfeng Catering Company in response to the evidence submitted by Qingfeng Baozi Shop, could prove that Xu Qingfeng once studied catering in Beijing and engaged in work related to the catering field.

In its retrial, this court held that the main issues in dispute between the parties during the retrial period were: (1) whether Qingfeng Catering Company's use of the characters "庆丰" on its website and at its business premises infringed the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop; (2) whether Qingfeng Catering Company's act of registering and using the characters "庆丰" as its enterprise trade name constituted unfair competition; (3) how Qingfeng Catering Company should bear civil liability.

I. Regarding the issue of whether Qingfeng Catering Company's use of the characters "庆丰" on its website and at its business premises infringed the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

Article 52, item (1) of the Trademark Law provides: "Using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the permission of the trademark registrant constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark." Article 1, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks provides: "Using characters that are identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the trade name of an enterprise in a prominent manner on the same or similar goods, which is likely to cause misidentification by the relevant public, constitutes other acts causing damage to the exclusive right to use another person's registered trademark as specified in Article 52, item (5) of the Trademark Law."

First, regarding the manner in which Qingfeng Catering Company used the characters "庆丰". Qingfeng Catering Company set up columns such as "Entering Qingfeng," "Qingfeng Culture," "Qingfeng Highlights," and "Qingfeng News" on its company website, and hung a banner reading "Qingfeng Catering welcomes all employees" at its business premises. The relevant public would perceive the characters "庆丰" as a mark distinguishing the source of goods or services. The use by Qingfeng Catering Company constituted prominent use of the "庆丰" trademark and constituted trademark use.

Second, regarding the reputation of the registered trademarks in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop. Based on the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, the "慶豐" trademark of Qingfeng Baozi Shop had been registered since January 28, 1998, until the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company on June 24, 2009, a period of more than ten years; the "老庆丰+lao qing feng" trademark was registered nearly six years before the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company. The chain stores of Qingfeng Baozi Shop were recognized by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Commerce in 2007 as "Chinese Specialty Flavor Restaurants." In 2007, Qingfeng Baozi Shop spent over RMB 1.31 million on advertising on Beijing radio and television, and from 2008 until before the establishment of Qingfeng Catering Company, it spent over RMB 3.22 million on advertising on those media. Qingfeng Baozi Shop adopted a nationwide chain operation model and, through years of honest operation and advertising, achieved high distinctiveness and reputation.

Third, regarding the assessment of the similarity between the characters "庆丰" used by Qingfeng Catering Company and the registered trademarks in question. The "慶豐" trademark registered by Qingfeng Baozi Shop for restaurant services, and the "老庆丰+lao qing feng" trademark registered for goods such as instant noodles, pastries, and steamed buns, had high reputation and influence nationwide. "慶豐" and "庆丰" are a one-to-one correspondence between traditional and simplified Chinese characters, with the same pronunciation; "老庆丰+lao qing feng" completely contains the characters "庆丰". Qingfeng Catering Company's use of the characters "庆丰" as a trademark in restaurant services, which are similar to the goods or services for which the above two registered trademarks of Qingfeng Baozi Shop are approved for use, is likely to cause the relevant public to be confused about the source of the goods or services or to believe that the source of Qingfeng Catering Company has a specific connection with Qingfeng Baozi Shop, potentially leading to confusion and misidentification.

Fourth, regarding the reasonableness assessment of Qingfeng Catering Company's use of the characters "庆丰". Qingfeng Catering Company argued that its use of the characters "庆丰" constituted a reasonable use of its enterprise trade name and a reasonable use of the name of its legal representative, Xu Qingfeng. In this regard, this court held that the legal representative of Qingfeng Catering Company is Xu Qingfeng, whose name contains the characters "庆丰". Xu Qingfeng enjoys the legitimate right to his name and may naturally use his own name reasonably. However, when Xu Qingfeng uses his name as a trademark or enterprise trade name for commercial purposes, he must not violate the principle of good faith and must not infringe upon the prior rights of others. Xu Qingfeng had worked in the Beijing catering industry and should have known the reputation and influence of the Qingfeng Baozi Shop trademark. Nevertheless, he prominently used trademarks that were identical or similar to the registered trademarks of Qingfeng Baozi Shop on his website and at his business premises, clearly demonstrating malicious intent to ride on the reputation of the Qingfeng Baozi Shop registered trademark, making it easy for the relevant public to be confused. This constitutes other acts causing damage to the exclusive right to use another person's registered trademark as specified in the aforementioned judicial interpretation. His actions do not constitute a reasonable use of the legal representative's name. Therefore, the alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company constituted an infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks in question of Qingfeng Baozi Shop. The findings of the courts of first and second instance that the alleged acts of Qingfeng Catering Company constituted reasonable use and did not constitute infringement were erroneous, and this court corrects them.

It should be pointed out that the Trademark Law of China encourages producers and operators to ensure the quality of goods and services through honest operation, to establish a reputation consistent with their own commercial goodwill, and to continuously enhance the brand value of their trademarks, while protecting the interests of consumers and producers/operators. Qingfeng Catering Company may register its own distinctive trademark, and through its own production, operation, and advertising, create and strengthen its own brand, establish commercial goodwill consistent with its brand, enhance its competitiveness, and promote the long-term development of the enterprise.

II. Regarding the issue of whether Qingfeng Catering Company's act of registering and using the characters "庆丰" as its enterprise trade name constituted unfair competition.

Article 5, item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "Using another person's enterprise name or personal name without authorization, leading people to mistakenly believe it is the goods of that other person, constitutes an act of unfair competition." Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Unfair Competition Civil Cases provides: "...The trade name of an enterprise name that has a certain degree of market reputation and is known to the relevant public may be recognized as the 'enterprise name' specified in Article 5, item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law."

Based on the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, Qingfeng Baozi Shop opened in 1956, began using the "庆丰" enterprise trade name on January 5, 1982, and had used it for over twenty-seven years by the date Qingfeng Catering Company was registered. It was a trade name in an enterprise name that had a high level of market reputation and was known to the relevant public. Qingfeng Catering Company, without authorization, used the trade name of Qingfeng Baozi Shop as its own trade name for registration and use, operating the same type of goods or services, with malicious intent to ride on the reputation of the Qingfeng Baozi Shop enterprise name. Its actions constituted unfair competition. The court of second instance erred in finding that the actions of Qingfeng Catering Company did not constitute unfair competition, and this court corrects this.

III. Regarding the issue of Qingfeng Catering Company's civil liability.

The alleged infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company constituted infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks of Qingfeng Baozi Shop and unfair competition, and it must bear civil liability for ceasing the above acts and compensating for losses. Because Qingfeng Baozi Shop did not provide evidence of the losses it suffered due to the above infringing acts of Qingfeng Catering Company or the profits gained by Qingfeng Catering Company, this court, taking into account factors such as the nature and severity of the infringing acts and the subjective mental state of Qingfeng Catering Company regarding the above infringing acts, determined by discretion that Qingfeng Catering Company should compensate Qingfeng Baozi Shop for economic losses and reasonable expenses in the amount of RMB 50,000. Because Qingfeng Baozi Shop failed to provide evidence proving that the goodwill of its trademark and enterprise reputation was damaged by the infringement and unfair competition acts of Qingfeng Catering Company, this court does not support its claim for Qingfeng Catering Company to publish a statement in the Jinan Daily to eliminate the adverse effects.

In summary, the retrial application of Qingfeng Baozi Shop meets the circumstances specified in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1 and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, judgment is rendered as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment No. (2014) Lumin San Zhong Zi No. 43 of the Shandong High People's Court;

2. Set aside the Civil Judgment No. (2013) Jimin San Chu Zi No. 716 of the Jinan Intermediate People's Court, Shandong Province;

3. Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease using the "庆丰" mark, which infringes the exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop, effective from the date this judgment takes effect;

4. Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease the unfair competition act of using the "庆丰" trade name in its enterprise name, effective from the date this judgment takes effect;

5. Within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. shall compensate Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop for economic losses and reasonable expenses in the amount of RMB 50,000;

6. Dismiss the other claims of Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop.

If the monetary payment obligation specified in this judgment is not performed within the period specified, a doubling of the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be paid in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances are each RMB 9,700, totaling RMB 19,400, of which Beijing Qingfeng Baozi Shop shall bear RMB 1,400 and Shandong Qingfeng Catering Management Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 18,000.

This judgment is final.
